polychoice: Multinomial Choice, Inflated Multinomial Logit, and Tests of IIA

Source: R/polychoice-package.R
polychoice-package.Rd

Estimation, inference, quantities of interest, and specification tests for unordered polytomous (multinomial) choice outcomes, behind one interface and one class of fitted objects ("choicemodel").

Estimators

mnl() fits the multinomial / conditional logit with case-specific covariates (alternative-specific coefficients), alternative-specific covariates (generic coefficients), alternative-specific constants, varying choice sets, frequency weights, offsets, unit fixed effects (with the split-panel jackknife bias_correct = "jackknife"), and analytic, outer-product, robust, cluster-robust, or bootstrap standard errors. imnl() fits the baseline-inflated multinomial logit of Bagozzi and Marchetti (2017) for any inflated alternative, with a logit or probit split equation, and with several inflated alternatives the parametrized logit captivity model of Swait and Ben-Akiva (1987), which generalizes the dogit of Gaudry and Dagenais (1979). nlogit() fits the two-level nested logit, hev() the heteroskedastic extreme value model, mnprobit() the multinomial probit with a free covariance, and remnl() the multinomial logit with random alternative-specific intercepts per unit; these accept a wide layout (one row per case) and a long layout (one row per case-alternative pair; see the id and alt arguments). rologit() fits the rank-ordered (exploded) logit to complete, partial, or tied rankings in the long layout.

Separation

separation() checks exactly, by a linear program, whether the data of an mnl() or rologit() fit are separated (no finite maximum-likelihood estimate). The maximum-likelihood likelihood-ratio tests then compare the suprema of the log-likelihoods. firth = TRUE (Firth's penalty) and prior = coef_prior(...) (normal, Cauchy or t priors) give finite penalized estimates, with profile intervals and penalized likelihood-ratio tests.

Quantities of interest and comparison

predict.choicemodel(), first_difference(), rrr(), fit_stats(), classification(), lr_test(), vuong(), boot_lr_test(), compare_models(), mundlak(), the simulators rmnl(), rnlogit(), rhev(), rmnp(), rrologit() and simulate.choicemodel(), and broom / texreg / modelsummary support.

Tests of the independence of irrelevant alternatives and of specification

hausman_mcfadden(), small_hsiao(), fp_tests() (Fok and Paap 2025), the battery iia_tests(), the nested-logit score test nested_lm_test() (McFadden 1987), combine_test() (Cramer and Ridder 1991), term_test(), the goodness-of-fit test hl_test() (Fagerland, Hosmer and Bofin 2008), the stability test of rank-ordered fits rank_test(), the score and likelihood-ratio tests for captive choosers captivity_test(), and the parametric-bootstrap calibration boot_pvalue().

Data

pa2006 and pres2004, the two applications of Bagozzi and Marchetti (2017), whose published fits are regression tests of the package, and seven data sets from published replication archives: sanctions, fluvax, bes1987, defection, bes2010, cabinets, and afghan_leaders (see the vignette "Seven published analyses").
